fields.name: timestamp_ns
fields.meaning: synthetic monotonic event time in ns; each event adds randint(50, 200); read but not used by the processing (Rust: #[allow(dead_code)])

fields.name: sensor_id
fields.meaning: sensor index 0..999, uniform randrange(1000); key of the per-sensor state hash map

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: measurement: baseline[sensor] + N(0,1) noise, or baseline +/- U(5,10) for an injected anomaly

generation.baselines: per sensor 10 + U(0,1)*80, i.e. U(10, 90), drawn first for all 1000 sensors
generation.per_event: ts += randint(50,200); sid = randrange(1000); with prob 0.02: value = baseline[sid] + sign*U(5,10), sign = +/-1 with p=0.5; else value = baseline[sid] + gauss(0,1)

detection.window_kind: per-sensor ring buffer of the last 128 values with running sum and sum of squares (rolling mean / variance, O(1) per event)
detection.warmup_meaning: no z-score test until the sensor has >= 32 values in its window
detection.rule: anomaly if |value - mean| > 3 * std, mean and population std over the window that already includes the current value; std = sqrt(max(0, (sum_sq - sum^2/n)/n))
detection.state: HashMap<u32, SensorState> (Rust) / HashMap<Integer, SensorState> (Java), entry created lazily on first event of a sensor

includes: reading and decoding one 20-byte record from a 64 KiB buffered reader (incl. the occasional refill syscall, ~every 3277 events)
Java: creation of the Event record object (possibly removed by JIT escape analysis)
hash-map lookup / insert of the sensor state
latency_measurement.histogram: 64 log2 buckets, bucket i = [100*2^i, 100*2^(i+1)) ns; percentiles reported as the bucket upper bound; exact min / max / mean kept separately
latency_measurement.reported: p50, p95, p99, p99.9, max, mean -> output/scenario4_latency_{lang}.json

notes: bench/config.toml describes scenario4 as '100M events', but the generator (EVENT_COUNT) and results (total_events = 1000000000) use 1e9
